# Naming Requirements Quality Checklist: Ship Names

**Purpose**: Validate that the ship-naming requirements are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and
measurable before `/speckit-tasks` turns them into work items. This checklist tests the
**requirements**, not the implementation.

**Created**: 2026-07-25

**Worked**: 2026-07-25—all 32 items resolved. 24 produced spec amendments; 8 were accepted as-is
with the reason recorded.

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Audience/timing**: Spec author, before task generation—while amendments are still cheap.

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context
and requirements. It complements [requirements.md](./requirements.md), which covers generic spec
quality; this one interrogates the naming domain specifically.

## Sourcing & Content-Risk Requirements

- [x] CHK001 Is "stand on their own outside their source work" defined with a decision procedure a
      contributor could apply to a borderline name, rather than left to judgement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]
  - **Accepted as-is.** The phrase is rationale; the operative test is the three-basis list that
    follows the colon, which FR-016a fixes as a closed set. A name qualifies iff it fits one of the
    three—that *is* the procedure.
- [x] CHK002 Is "distinctive coined names identified with a particular work or franchise" given
      objective exclusion criteria, or is the boundary between it and FR-016's three permitted bases
      left to the cataloguer? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016]
  - **Amended.** Real trap: *Serenity* is an ordinary word but strongly identified with one show,
    so the two sentences could be read as contradicting each other. FR-016 now states that
    qualifying under a basis is decisive—an independent basis means the name was not coined.
- [x] CHK003 Do the requirements state whether the recorded basis must be *true*, or only
      *well-formed*? FR-016b's automatic check proves presence and set-membership; is a
      correctness-review requirement defined anywhere? [Gap, Spec §FR-016b, §SC-007]
  - **Amended.** Added **FR-016c**: the reference must be specific enough to confirm without
    repeating the research, and every fiction entry is reviewed against its basis when added.
    FR-016b proves *well-formed*; FR-016c is what makes it *true*.
- [x] CHK004 Is "public-domain work" scoped to a jurisdiction and/or date, given that public-domain
      status is jurisdiction-dependent? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-016a]
  - **Amended.** FR-016a now judges public-domain status under United States copyright law. No
    content cost: every candidate in research.md C3 predates it by a century or more.
- [x] CHK005 Is "a short reference naming the specific word, vessel, or work" bounded by any format
      or length constraint that would make it consistently reviewable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016a]
  - **Amended via CHK003.** FR-016c's "specific enough to confirm without repeating the research"
    is the right constraint; a character count would not have been.
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for a name that qualifies under more than one basis kind —
      must one be chosen, and by what rule? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-016a]
  - **Amended.** FR-016a: exactly one kind is recorded, the most direct where several apply. The
    rule existed only in research.md C1 (the *Nautilus* case).
- [x] CHK007 Does the spec specify how a name belonging to two traditions is assigned (e.g. a
      mythological name a franchise later used)? The rule exists in data-model.md but has no
      requirement backing it in the spec. [Gap, Spec §FR-007, Data-model "Assignment rule"]
  - **Amended.** Added **FR-007a**: earliest tradition wins, catalogued exactly once. Without it
    FR-009 (no duplicates) had no stated tie-break, and this rule materially shapes the fiction
    traditions.
- [x] CHK008 Does exempting mythology and folklore from FR-016a leave an unstated assumption that
      no mythological name carries independent trademark or content risk? Is that assumption
      recorded? [Assumption, Spec §FR-016a]
  - **Amended.** Assumption added: these names are ancient and in common cultural use, so no work
    has a claim on them, and a coinciding modern trademark does not create one.
- [x] CHK009 Are requirements defined for removing or replacing a catalogue entry that is later
      found to be mis-sourced, including the consequence for previously-shared seeds?
      [Gap, Recovery Flow]
  - **Amended.** FR-010b plus a new Edge Case make withdrawal explicitly safe: the seed's *name*
    may change, its *ship* may not.
- [x] CHK010 Are content-suitability requirements (beyond sourcing) defined for catalogue entries,
      or is sourcing the only admissibility test? [Gap, Coverage]
  - **Accepted as-is.** No requirement added. Editorial curation of a 160-entry literal does not
    need a rule to be exercised, and inventing an admissibility test with no concrete failure in
    view is the speculative abstraction the constitution's simplicity posture rules out.

## Determinism & Additivity Requirements

- [x] CHK011 Do FR-010 ("same seed MUST produce the same name") and the catalogue's stated openness
      to growth conflict? Is the scope of FR-010—within one build, or across versions—stated?
      [Conflict, Spec §FR-010, §FR-008]
  - **Amended.** Genuine conflict. FR-010 is now scoped "for a given catalogue", which reconciles
    it with FR-008's growth allowance and with FR-010b.
- [x] CHK012 Is it stated as a requirement whether the seed-to-*name* mapping is a compatibility
      surface? The contract declares it is not; the spec was silent. [Gap, Contracts §Stability]
  - **Amended.** Added **FR-010b**, promoting the contract's stability note into a requirement:
    seed→name is not a compatibility surface, seed→ship is. This was the single most load-bearing
    gap on the list.
- [x] CHK013 Is SC-008's "every seed whose output was pinned" quantified—how many seeds, drawn
      how, covering which generation paths—so the criterion is objectively verifiable?
      [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
  - **Amended.** SC-008 now requires a corpus of at least 50 seeds *per generation path*. The
    already-captured `baseline/designs.json` (seeds 0–49 on both paths) satisfies it exactly.
- [x] CHK014 Does FR-010a enumerate what "identical in every other respect" covers, or is the
      "hull, drives, fittings, armament" list illustrative rather than exhaustive?
      [Clarity, Spec §FR-010a]
  - **Amended.** FR-010a now binds *every field of the design other than the name*, with the
    four-item list demoted to examples. The old wording could be read as permitting drift in an
    unlisted field.
- [x] CHK015 Are FR-011's claims that a name can be "recorded, replayed, and audited" backed by
      acceptance criteria, or are they descriptive prose with nothing to verify?
      [Measurability, Spec §FR-011]
  - **Amended.** FR-011 restated operatively: same randomness mechanism, no separate entropy
    source, no other route from the seed, and a scripted sequence must be able to pin the name.
    All four are checkable; "auditable" was not.
- [x] CHK016 Are the paths that produce a random ship enumerated, so "naming reaches every path"
      is checkable rather than open-ended? [Coverage, Spec Assumptions, §FR-002]
  - **Amended.** FR-002 and the Assumption now state that starships and small craft are the only
    kinds random generation produces, closing the set.
- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for generation with no seed supplied—does additivity apply
      only to seeded runs, and is that stated? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-010a]
  - **Accepted as-is.** FR-001 is unconditional and already covers unseeded runs; additivity is
    only meaningful relative to a pinned seed, so scoping FR-010a to seeds is correct as written.

## Catalogue Composition & Data Quality Requirements

- [x] CHK018 Is "duplicate" defined for FR-009—exact match, or normalised for case, whitespace,
      and punctuation? Without it, near-duplicates satisfy the requirement.
      [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-009]
  - **Amended, with a deliberate strengthening.** FR-009 now compares after stripping and
    case-folding, so "Odin" and "ODIN" cannot both be catalogued—which the previously-specified
    case-sensitive comparison would have allowed. data-model.md V7, contracts V7 and research.md
    Part E updated to match.
- [x] CHK019 Is the "no tradition exceeds half the catalogue" cap expressed as a functional
      requirement, or does it exist only as a success criterion with no FR to trace to?
      [Consistency, Gap, Spec §SC-005, §FR-008]
  - **Amended.** The cap now sits in FR-008 alongside the floors, so SC-005 measures a stated
    requirement rather than introducing one.
- [x] CHK020 Are the "ship-type designations" FR-017 forbids enumerated, or is the prohibition
      stated only by example ("Free Trader Beowulf")? [Clarity, Gap, Spec §FR-017]
  - **Accepted as-is.** FR-017 states a rule, not an example. The concrete deny-list is a design
    artefact and correctly lives in research.md Part E, where it can grow without a spec change.
- [x] CHK021 Is "plain unaccented spellings" specified as a concrete rule (e.g. an ASCII
      constraint, or a transliteration procedure), and does it cover names whose source is
      non-Latin script? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018]
  - **Amended.** FR-018 now requires romanisation for other scripts and ASCII-only entries. The
    catalogue draws on Japanese, Chinese, West African and Mesoamerican sources, so the non-Latin
    case is live, not hypothetical.
- [x] CHK022 Are constraints on name length and multi-word names specified, given that names are
      interpolated into a rendered description and an exported file? [Gap, Spec §FR-017, §FR-012]
  - **Amended.** Added **FR-018a**: multi-word names allowed, single spaces only, no leading,
    trailing or other whitespace. "Cu Chulainn" is in the sampled set, so this needed saying.
- [x] CHK023 Are FR-008's floors (≥150 total, ≥20 per tradition) and SC-005's cap jointly
      satisfiable, and is that consistency asserted rather than assumed?
      [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §SC-005]
  - **Verified consistent; no change.** Three traditions × 20 = 60 ≤ 150, and the cap is
    satisfiable at any size (the planned 76/42/42 puts the largest at 47.5%).
- [x] CHK024 Does FR-007 tie the recorded tradition to the closed set named in Key Entities, so
      "source tradition in scope" is enumerable rather than open? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
  - **Amended.** FR-007 now cites the fixed set of three, which also gives FR-008's per-tradition
    floor a definite denominator.

## Integration, Rendering & Round-Trip Requirements

- [x] CHK025 Is FR-012's "wherever the description already refers to the ship by name" verifiable
      without reading the implementation—are the referring locations identified?
      [Measurability, Spec §FR-012]
  - **Accepted as-is.** The requirement is an equivalence: a generated name behaves exactly as an
    author-supplied name already does. That is testable by comparison without enumerating
    locations, and it stays correct if the description gains another mention.
- [x] CHK026 Is the blank/whitespace-only-name behaviour stated as a requirement, or does it exist
      only as an edge-case narrative with no FR to trace to? [Gap, Traceability, Spec Edge Cases]
  - **Amended.** Added **FR-015a**: an empty or whitespace-only name is no name, and renders as
    "Unnamed Ship".
- [x] CHK027 Do FR-001's qualifier "when the requester has not specified one" and the Assumptions'
      "no name-override option on the generator" conflict—is there any path by which a requester
      can specify a name at generation time? [Conflict, Spec §FR-001, Assumptions]
  - **Amended.** There is no such path, so the qualifier described a dead branch. FR-001 is now
    unconditional and points at FR-014 for the design-supplied case.
- [x] CHK028 Are FR-014 and FR-015 distinguishable, or do they state the same guarantee twice from
      different angles? Is each independently testable? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014, §FR-015]
  - **Accepted as-is.** They test different halves: FR-014 with a named design (renders that name),
    FR-015 with a nameless one (renders "Unnamed Ship"). Overlapping, not redundant.
- [x] CHK029 Is SC-001's "'Unnamed Ship' never appears in random generation output" consistent with
      the Assumptions' retention of the fallback, and is the boundary between the two paths stated
      unambiguously? [Consistency, Spec §SC-001, Assumptions]
  - **Accepted as-is.** SC-001 is scoped to random generation; the fallback belongs to designs.
    The two are disjoint and both say so.

## Acceptance Criteria Quality, Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK030 Is SC-003 ("at least 17 of 20 distinct") specified with the seeds or sampling method
      it is measured over, so the criterion is deterministic rather than statistical?
      [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
  - **Amended.** SC-003 now names a fixed, documented seed set. As written it would have become a
    test that could pass or fail from run to run.
- [x] CHK031 Is the Assumptions' "repeats within a normal batch are uncommon" reconciled with
      SC-003's threshold, or are two different tolerances stated for the same property?
      [Consistency, Spec Assumptions, §SC-003]
  - **Amended.** The Assumption now defers to SC-003 as the operative measure of "uncommon".
- [x] CHK032 Is the dependency on the existing design-name field and its prose-validation rules
      documented as an assumption, given that a catalogue entry rejected by that validation would
      break naming? [Dependency, Gap, Data-model V6]
  - **Amended.** Assumption added, and FR-018a restates the whitespace constraint at spec level so
    the catalogue cannot introduce a name the renderer would refuse.

## Notes

- Check items off as completed: `[x]`
- Record findings inline; each finding is either a spec amendment or an explicit
  "accepted as-is, because…" note.
- Items marked `[Gap]` ask whether a requirement exists at all; items marked `[Conflict]` or
  `[Ambiguity]` ask whether an existing one is sound.
- Several items pointed at content that lived only in `plan.md`, `data-model.md`, or
  `contracts/name-catalogue.md`. Design documents may legitimately hold the mechanism, but a
  guarantee a consumer depends on belongs in the spec—that reasoning drove CHK007, CHK012 and
  CHK019.
